terms.label: Root mean square
terms.plain: RMS is the square root of the mean squared signal.
terms.meaning: For a pure sine only, peak amplitude is √2 times RMS. For a fixed resistor, RMS determines average heating.
cautions: RMS is not the arithmetic mean or a universal peak conversion.

terms.label: Peak amplitude
terms.plain: Peak amplitude is the largest excursion from zero.
terms.meaning: The imported R1/R2/R3 electrical phasors use peak amplitude, while the host circuit inputs use RMS.
cautions: Sample peak, reconstructed true peak and acoustic pressure peak are different measurements.

terms.label: Phase and coherent readout
terms.plain: Phase locates one repeating signal relative to another.
terms.meaning: Coherent complex readout preserves relative amplitude and phase under a declared shared reference.
cautions: Sharing a sample clock does not establish equal gain, stable transfer or calibration.

terms.label: Calibration and deterministic error bounds
terms.plain: Calibration connects instrument readings with a stated reference.
terms.meaning: These contracts supply deterministic error radii in volts, amperes, henries or dimensionless transfer units, as declared.
cautions: A stipulated error radius is not measured sensor performance or a confidence interval.

terms.label: Drift, pilot and cross-talk
terms.plain: A reference tone can help notice changes during a recording.
terms.meaning: Pilot drift can arise in the source, path or recorder; pre-roll records the background before excitation, and cross-talk mixes channels.
cautions: A stable pilot is not a calibration certificate; two microphones do not guarantee isolation.

terms.label: Clipping and bandwidth
terms.plain: A recorder can cut off large signals or miss frequencies.
terms.meaning: Clipping limits waveform amplitude; bandwidth declares which frequencies a system can represent with stated accuracy.
cautions: A non-clipping trace alone does not establish calibrated response.

terms.label: Not to scale
terms.plain: A sketch may show relationships without preserving size ratios.
terms.meaning: Use written dimensions and declared coordinate units rather than measuring screen pixels.
cautions: An accurate-looking diagram is not an engineering drawing or a calibrated photograph.

terms.label: Frequency and period
terms.plain: Frequency counts repeating cycles each second.
terms.meaning: A period is one cycle duration; f=1/T. A recorded spectrum can contain many peaks.
cautions: Frequency f differs from force F; a monument does not automatically have one scalar frequency.

terms.label: Acoustic pressure
terms.plain: Sound pressure is a changing pressure measured in air.
terms.meaning: Pressure spectra, electrical voltage, displacement and digital sample amplitude are different channels.
cautions: The synthetic room model is relative digital amplitude, not calibrated Pa or dB SPL.

terms.label: Path distance, delay and sound speed
terms.plain: Longer sound paths arrive later.
terms.meaning: The early-reflection model uses t=d/c with c=343 m/s unless otherwise declared.
cautions: This c is sound speed, not vacuum light speed or capacitance C.

terms.label: SI and unit prefixes
terms.plain: SI is the international system of measurement units.
terms.meaning: cm=0.01 m, mm=0.001 m, µ=10⁻⁶, milli=10⁻³ and nano=10⁻⁹ of the stated unit.
cautions: A source drawing in cm or mm is not silently a metres-based parts table.

terms.label: Scalable Vector Graphics
terms.plain: SVG stores a drawing as shapes and text.
terms.meaning: A vector drawing can retain dimensions and annotations independently of display resolution.
cautions: A precise-looking SVG is not a validated construction drawing.

terms.label: JavaScript Object Notation
terms.plain: JSON stores structured data that can be exported and inspected.
terms.meaning: A receipt encodes declared inputs, outputs and provenance as text records.
cautions: Serialization does not authenticate a claim or measure a device.

terms.label: SHA-256 content digest
terms.plain: A digest helps compare whether two files have the same bytes.
terms.meaning: SHA means Secure Hash Algorithm; the digest identifies content under the named algorithm.
cautions: A matching digest proves neither the truth of content nor its author.

terms.label: Fast Fourier transform
terms.unit: frequency bins in Hz; amplitude units declared separately
terms.plain: A Fourier transform separates a sampled waveform into frequency components.
terms.meaning: FFT is an efficient algorithm for the discrete Fourier transform; bin spacing is sample rate divided by transform length.
cautions: A spectral peak is not necessarily the fundamental, a material mode or calibrated acoustic pressure.

terms.label: Pulse-code modulation and sampling
terms.plain: PCM represents a waveform as a sequence of numbered samples.
terms.meaning: PCM16 encodes signed 16-bit samples; sample rate sets the time interval. Frequencies must stay below half the sample rate.
cautions: A 48 kHz sample rate is not the pitch of the sound.

terms.label: Decibels relative to digital full scale
terms.plain: dBFS expresses digital signal level below the largest sample value.
terms.meaning: For normalized amplitude A, level is 20 log10(|A|). A −24 dBFS master is a digital gain choice.
cautions: It is not calibrated sound-pressure level or a guarantee of safe ear exposure.
